early-blight.name: Early Blight
early-blight.description: Brown circular spots with concentric rings, commonly starting on older lower leaves.
biological: Remove infected leaves and dispose of them away from the planting area.
Improve airflow by pruning dense foliage and spacing plants properly.
chemical: Use a tomato-safe fungicide according to the product label when disease pressure is high.
prevention: Mulch around plants to reduce soil splash.
Rotate tomato crops away from the same soil for future seasons.

late-blight.name: Late Blight
late-blight.description: Fast-spreading dark, water-soaked lesions that can collapse leaves and stems in humid weather.
biological: Remove badly infected plants quickly to reduce spread.
Keep foliage dry and improve ventilation around plants.
chemical: Apply a labeled protective fungicide early when local late blight risk is high.
prevention: Avoid working with plants while leaves are wet.
Destroy volunteer tomato or potato plants nearby.

leaf-mold.name: Leaf Mold
leaf-mold.description: Yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces with fuzzy mold growth underneath, especially in humid areas.
biological: Remove affected leaves and reduce humidity around the crop.
Increase spacing and airflow in greenhouse or covered growing areas.
chemical: Use a labeled fungicide if symptoms continue after humidity control.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant.

healthy-tomato-leaf.name: Healthy Tomato Leaf
healthy-tomato-leaf.description: The uploaded leaf appears healthy based on the model prediction.
prevention: Continue regular inspection for spots, discoloration, or wilting.
Maintain consistent watering and balanced nutrition.

non-tomato-leaf.name: Non-Tomato Leaf
non-tomato-leaf.description: The uploaded image does not appear to be a tomato leaf.
prevention: Upload a clear tomato leaf image in good lighting for best results.
